items.title: BIG MOVE: Applied Materials Bets $5 Billion on India's Semiconductor Future at Semicon India 2026
items.summary:
This massive $5 billion investment from Applied Materials will significantly reshape the semiconductor landscape in India.

The company is building a 140-acre semiconductor research park near the Bengaluru airport, positioning the region as a critical hub for global chip-making equipment. This initiative aims to expand the local supply chain capacity ten-fold by 2035, moving beyond simple design to end-to-end product development.

Beyond the new bangalore tech park, the expansion includes new innovation centers in Chennai and Mumbai, plus a support hub in Gujarat. For those tracking the stock market, this move highlights how global equipment manufacturers are diversifying their operations to integrate Indian engineering into the broader semiconductor value chain.

items.title: An AI That Interrupts You on Purpose
items.summary: In episode 1027 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Dilani Kahawala, Co-Founder and CEO of Anna, about how Anna works as a long-running agent instead of sitting and waiting for you to type. She explains how it works constantly in the background, checking email, filtering out noise and working out which kid a task is for, then interjects when a changed meeting is about to clash with school pickup.

items.title: BREAKTHROUGH: GPT-6 Cracked a 108-Year-Old WWI Military Cipher Hidden Since 1918
items.summary:
GPT-6 Astra successfully cracked a 108-year-old German radio code, exposing lost intelligence about WWI-era British warship movements.

OpenAI's latest model demonstrated its ability to perform autonomous research by reading archival scans and verifying the data against original HMS Canterbury logbooks. The AI even resolved ambiguous characters in the cipher grid to confirm historical ship arrival dates from 1918. This breakthrough highlights the growing sophistication of AI models in historical analysis and complex data reconstruction.

Beyond historical research, this capability mirrors the specific cybersecurity risk OpenAI identified regarding autonomous code-breaking. By using a self-verification loop, the model reconstructed transposition systems and searched databases to correct its own errors, a method also used to solve a 1941 Enigma message in just 10 hours. As these tools become more capable, the boundary between research assistance and critical security vulnerability continues to blur.

items.title: The Chip Built for Agentic AI Inference, with SambaNova's Anton McGonnell (Ep. 1028)
items.summary:
In Episode #1028, Anton McGonnell (VP of Product at SambaNova) joins @JonKrohnLearns to explain why the chips running most AI inference today were never designed for the job. Agentic AI has changed the computational profile of inference, with much larger inputs and far heavier caches feeding the token generation that follows, and that shift has exposed where GPU architecture struggles. SambaNova has raised over $2 billion to build an alternative, the reconfigurable dataflow unit, which lays a whole model out spatially across the chip rather than executing it kernel by kernel. In this episode, Anton discusses why the speed that matters is payback, and how speed and concurrency are what turn a fixed hardware cost into a six-month payback. He also walks through the trade-off every inference provider faces between speed per user and throughput per chip, what the RDU architecture changes about scaling and data center deployment, the economics of the new SN50, and why four out of five AI infrastructure leaders say they would pay a premium for faster tokens.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:02:41) Why agentic AI is reshaping inference workloads
• (00:08:39) How SambaNova's RDU differs from a GPU
• (00:17:54) The economics of the SN50

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1028
